editorial:
Imagine a world where being single is illegal, and you only have 45 days to find a partner before you become an animal. That is the strange setup of this dark comedy, where Colin Farrell plays a quiet man named David who checks into a strict hotel after his wife leaves him. The hotel staff push guests to pair up fast, and the rules feel both funny and unsettling. You watch David try to fit in, make awkward connections, and face a choice between forcing a match or escaping into the woods with lonely rebels. The vibe is dry, weird, and oddly touching, with deadpan humor that makes you laugh even when things get uncomfortable.

The acting is excellent, especially Farrell’s flat, sad delivery and Rachel Weisz’s warm, sharp presence. The pacing is slow but steady, and the story keeps surprising you with strange twists. Some scenes feel cold or repetitive, and the humor will not work for everyone. If you like odd, thoughtful movies that mix romance with satire, this is a great pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, David and his short-sighted partner pretend to be a normal couple in the city. To prove his love and match her disability, he takes a steak knife into the bathroom and prepares to blind himself. The movie ends before showing whether he actually does it, leaving you with an unsettling question about how far people will go to fit in and stay together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird, thoughtful comedies with a dark edge.
